answer: A Sybil-resistant check could use mesa orchard stewardship tied to umber soil. Each applicant gets one orchard row on a named mesa terrace and, over a season, must prune it, record fruit set, and submit soil whose umber hue and mineral profile match that terrace. Growth and harvest timing vary by terrace, so a scripted farm cannot precompute convincing logs. One person cannot credibly tend many distant terraces. Neighbouring growers verify logs against their own plots, so many fake identities would need many real growers, while an honest participant tends a nearby row.
